The comment says this event is logged “for debugging only”, but the code logs at INFO level. If this is an expected customer-configuration state, INFO may be too noisy in production logs; consider using DEBUG (or adjust the comment if INFO is intentional).
```suggestion
                self._logger.debug("Edge appliance not set up - returning empty S3 Edge statuses: %s", err_msg)
```

author: Copilot
body: _get_services reimplements the repo’s standard concurrent-awaitable pattern (gather + exception propagation). Since the codebase already has gather_tasks_and_propagate_exceptions() (documented as the Sentry-safe approach) and it’s used elsewhere in this repo, consider wrapping only the S3-edge call (catching the specific ResourceConflict and returning an empty status) and then using gather_tasks_and_propagate_exceptions for the actual concurrency. This avoids subtle behavioral drift (e.g., exception ordering/handling) and keeps the Sentry-related logic centralized.

author: Copilot
body: This test’s docstring says it covers an alternate/plaintext NOC error message, but the mocked error string is the same as `NocClientErrorMessages.edge_appliance_needed.value` (just inlined). That makes this test largely redundant with the previous one and doesn’t validate handling of a genuinely different message format. Consider either using a distinct message variant that should still be treated as "no edge appliance" (or parameterize both cases), or adjust the test name/docstring to reflect what’s actually being tested.

author: Copilot
body: `_get_s3_edge_statuses` now converts the `edge_appliance_needed` `ResourceConflict` into an empty `NocS3ScubeStatusResponse`. Given `noc.api.client.NocClient.get_edges_s3_edge_statuses()` is the only place that raises this specific error, the existing `ResourceConflict` handlers in `get_edges`/`get_edge` that special-case `edge_appliance_needed` look to be unreachable now and risk becoming misleading/dead code. Consider removing those branches (or updating them to reflect the new behavior) so the error-handling contract is defined in one place.

author: Copilot
body: The test name/docstring says "empty S3" and mentions returning the "filer list", but the assertions validate `edge.services.s3_edge is None` (i.e., S3 Edge status unavailable) and the subject is edges. Renaming the test (and adjusting wording) to reflect `s3_edge=None` and "edge list" would make the intent clearer and avoid confusion about whether an explicit empty status object is expected.
